title: fm board recognises and replaces a board this checkout started even while the board is busy: the root check waits for a slow board instead of reading a two-second silence as a foreign or dead listener, so a merged board change no longer needs a hand kill
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05/06, after T-215, T-221 and T-222 merged, every `bin/fm.sh board` (bin/fm.sh:853 -> `python3 bin/fm-herdr.py board <repo>`) exited 70 with 'fm board: the board on :4173 runs old code or is not answering and cannot be replaced; stop it (kill <pid>) and run fm board', although the listener was the board this checkout started (`/opt/homebrew/bin/bun run /Users/benjamin/Desktop/firstmate-workflow/board/server.ts`, started by fm board under the session lifeline). Firstmate killed it by hand each time; the next fm board then started a fresh board at once. The T-209 drain-and-replace path never ran.

Mechanism (root cause, measured on the live board, read-only). The board's request handling runs synchronous work: `/api/state` takes about 2.1 s per call (curl time_total 2.09-2.16 s on main c00e5cf), during which Bun's event loop answers nothing else; the open board page fetches `/api/state` repeatedly (board/public/index.html:439, :899, :919, :1022). A `/file` request that alone takes about 0.001 s took 1.99 s while one `/api/state` was in flight and 4.50 s while two were. `board_matches` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2128-2138) probes `/file?path=state/session/probe-<uuid>` through `http_get` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2120-2125), whose `urlopen(..., timeout=2)` raises a timeout (an OSError) that `board_matches` turns into False. `board_start` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2437-) then takes the not-reused branch into `fresh_start`, whose `http_get(url)` also times out at 2 s (OSError), `board_listening(port)` is True, and it raises `BoardRefusal(port, board_port_pid(port))` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2449-2450) — the message above. The code-identity comparison and `board_drain` are never reached, so a busy own board looks like a foreign or dead one. After a hand kill no page is polling the new board yet, so its probe answers in time.

Change 1 (patient root check). In bin/fm-herdr.py, `http_get` takes an optional keyword `timeout` (default stays 2 s, so every other caller is unchanged). `board_matches(root, url)` keeps writing one fresh random nonce file per call and deleting it in `finally`, but asks with a per-try timeout of 5 s and asks again with the same nonce only when the try timed out, until a total budget of 20 s (module constants, for example `BOARD_PROBE_TRY = 5` and `BOARD_PROBE_BUDGET = 20`, measured with time.monotonic). `board_matches` takes an optional keyword `budget` (default `BOARD_PROBE_BUDGET`). Deadline rule: the deadline is fixed at the first try (start + budget); each try's timeout is `min(BOARD_PROBE_TRY, deadline - now)`; no new try starts once `deadline - now <= 0`; a reply that a started try does return is judged on its body even when it arrives after the deadline (a matching nonce is True). So the whole check never asks past the deadline plus nothing, and never longer than the budget. A timed-out try is exactly: a `TimeoutError` (which `socket.timeout` is), or a `urllib.error.URLError` whose `.reason` is a `TimeoutError` — urlopen wraps socket errors in URLError, so a refused connection arrives as `URLError(reason=ConnectionRefusedError)` and must be read through `.reason`. Each retry follows a timeout, which has already waited up to 5 s, so the loop cannot spin; no extra sleep is added. It returns True only for a reply equal to the nonce, and returns False at once (no further try) for any other reply body, an HTTPError, any other OSError or URLError (a refused, reset or denied connection, whether bare or inside URLError.reason) or a ValueError, and returns False when the budget ends. The existing contract stays: the path is relative, and a definite wrong-root answer costs exactly one request (tests/session.test.sh:25-37 asserts `len(seen) == 1`).

Change 2 (the other waits in board_start use the same patience). In `board_start`, the `fresh_start` occupancy probe `http_get(url)` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2447) and the final `page = bool(http_get(url))` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2523) pass `timeout=BOARD_PROBE_TRY`, so a busy board is reported as occupied by an unverified root (or, when it still says nothing after a full try, as not answering) only after a real wait, and a busy verified board is not turned into an OSError traceback after a successful replacement. The verify loop after a fresh start (`for _ in range(50)` at :2465-2468) and the stop-wait loop (:2496-2506) are unchanged. `board_drain` keeps its 5 s timeout. `board_check_port` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2333-2343, used by bin/fm-setup.sh:174 through `board-check-port`) keeps today's single short check: it calls `board_matches(root, url, budget=2)` with the per-try timeout 2 s, so setup against a silent listener still refuses within about 2 s and tests/settings.test.sh:74-89 (`timeout=15`, 'unverified root', config unchanged) keeps passing unchanged. Session start (bin/fm-herdr.py:2989, `report['board'] = board_start(root)`) gets the same behaviour with no change of its own.

What stays refused (T-209/T-214 rules unchanged). A listener that answers the nonce wrongly, answers with an HTTP error, or stays silent for the whole 20 s budget is still never reused: it keeps the 'unverified root' error or the BoardRefusal with its pid and manual step, in English and Chinese, exit 70. A verified board with older code still goes through `board_drain`: a 409 (a merge running or an answer in flight) still leaves it in place with the existing 'run fm board again when it ends' notice; a board that is not session-owned or will not stop within ten seconds still gets the existing manual notice. A board of another checkout can never pass, because the nonce file is written under this root only.

Test (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify). In tests/session.test.sh (Python unittest inside the bash suite, the module loaded as `m`), add a test that patches `m.http_get` with a callable accepting `(url, **kw)` that raises `TimeoutError()` on its first call and returns the nonce file's bytes on the second, and patches `m.time.monotonic` (or the budget constant) so no real waiting happens: `m.board_matches(repo, 'http://127.0.0.1:4173')` is True and http_get was called twice with the same path. On base this is red: base `board_matches` returns False after the first TimeoutError. Add further assertions in the same test: a callable that always raises TimeoutError makes `board_matches` False once the (patched) budget ends; `URLError(TimeoutError())` once then the nonce gives True after two calls; `URLError(ConnectionRefusedError())`, `ConnectionResetError()` and b'wrong root' each give False after exactly one call. Add a `board_start` case in the style of `test_board_held_port_refusal_and_free_port_launch` (tests/session.test.sh:315-354): with `board_matches` real, `http_get` timing out once and then answering the nonce and `b'page'`, a recorded `code` equal to the current code, `board_start` returns `reused: True` and raises no BoardRefusal and starts no child (`lifeline().start` not called). Timeout values are asserted, not assumed: (i) patch `m.urllib.request.urlopen` and check `http_get(url)` forwards `timeout=2` and `http_get(url, timeout=5)` forwards 5; (ii) in the retry test, record the `timeout` keyword of each `board_matches` try: the first is 5 and, with monotonic patched so 17 s have passed, the next is 3 (the remaining budget), and with 20 s passed no further try is made; a matching reply returned by a try whose clock reads past the deadline is still True; (iii) `board_check_port` passes `budget=2` (patch board_matches and check the keyword); (iv) in the board_start case, record the `timeout` keyword of the `fresh_start` occupancy `http_get(url)` (reach it with `board_matches` False and a refused listener, as at tests/session.test.sh:342-346) and of the final page `http_get(url)`: both are 5. The wrong-root count is asserted with a counting callable (tests/session.test.sh:35-37 today counts only the matching mock's calls): b'wrong root' makes exactly one call. The existing refusal test keeps passing unchanged in meaning (it mocks `board_matches` False and `http_get` TimeoutError).

Callers and mocks checked (grep `http_get`, `board_matches`, `board_start`, `BoardRefusal` in bin/ and tests/). Production: bin/fm-herdr.py:2120 (def), :2133 (board_matches), :2342 (board_check_port), :2444/:2466/:2468 (board_start verify), :2447/:2499/:2523 (board_start gets), :2907 (main `board`), :2989 (session start); bin/fm.sh:853 and bin/fm-setup.sh:174 call the CLI only. Test mocks of `http_get` whose callables take one positional argument and would break on a new keyword: tests/session.test.sh:27 (`def request(url)`) and :254 (`def get(url)`) — give them `**kw` (or call `http_get` positionally where the timeout is not needed; say which). Mocks with `return_value`/`side_effect` lists (tests/session.test.sh:35, :136, :143, :166, :180, :321, :374, :544, :796; tests/settings.test.sh:56) accept any arguments and stay as they are, except that a list `side_effect` consumed by a retrying `board_matches` must still line up: check :166 (`[OSError(), b'page']` with `board_matches` mocked) and :796 (`[OSError('nothing there'), b'page']`) — `board_matches` is mocked there, so the retry does not consume them. tests/settings.test.sh:55, :95, :98 mock `board_matches` directly and are unaffected; tests/settings.test.sh:74-89 runs the real setup check against a silent listener and stays green because `board_check_port` keeps a 2 s budget. Also unaffected (checked): tests/session-startup.test.sh:23, tests/setup.test.sh:26 and tests/lib/session_fixture.py:16-24.

Design (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §11 'Self-update' (design.md:2635), subsection '### Managed session defaults' (design.md:2676), the paragraph that begins 'Board reuse is verified with a fresh random file under the requested root' (design.md:2701-2722): after 'a different or unverifiable root is refused.' add that `fm board` and session start wait for a busy board — each try up to 5 seconds, repeated only after a timed-out try, for up to 20 seconds in all — because the board answers nothing while it builds `/api/state`; any answer other than the nonce, an HTTP error, any other connection failure (refused, reset or denied) or a malformed address ends the check at once as unverified, and so do 20 seconds of silence. Setup's port check keeps a single 2-second try. The later sentence 'A listener that does not answer the root check in time is never mistaken for a free port' stays true and stays.

Out of scope: making `/api/state` faster or asynchronous (the 2 s synchronous build is a separate problem; note it in the PR), the drain protocol and `/drain` endpoint, the secret, the sign-in opener, the lifeline, and board/server.ts.
